chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'and he was a Messenger, a Prophet' — what is the Messenger and what is the Prophet? He said: The Prophet is the one who sees in his dream and hears the voice but does not directly behold the Angel; and the Messenger is the one who hears the voice, sees in the dream, and directly beholds the Angel.
I said: The Imam — what is his rank? He said: He hears the voice but does not see (in dream) and does not directly behold the Angel.
Then he recited this verse: 'And We did not send before you any Messenger, nor Prophet, nor Muhaddath.'

key_terms.رَسُولٌ: Rasool/Messenger — one who receives revelation and directly beholds the Angel of Revelation
key_terms.مَنَامٌ: dream/sleep — the mode of vision for the Nabi but not the Imam
key_terms.مَنْزِلَةٌ: rank/station — the divinely-assigned position in the hierarchy of divine communication
key_terms.مُحَدَّثٌ: Muhaddath — one spoken to by the divine voice; the Imam's mode of receiving divine communication
key_terms.نَبِيٌّ: Nabi/Prophet — one who receives revelation through dreams and the voice, without directly seeing the Angel
key_terms.يُعَايِنُ: to directly behold/see face-to-face — the highest form of reception of revelation

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a Rasool (Messenger), a Nabi (Prophet), and an Imam according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) explains the theological distinction between three degrees of prophetic and divine communication: the Nabi (prophet) receives revelation through dreams and hears the divine voice but does not see the Angel of Revelation; the Rasool (messenger) additionally sees the Angel directly; while the Imam (here termed Muhaddath, 'one spoken to') hears the divine voice alone, without dreams or direct vision of the Angel. The Imam supports this hierarchy by citing a Quranic verse (22:52) that, in the Shia recension, includes 'Muhaddath' as a third category alongside Rasool and Nabi — establishing the Imamate as a distinct divinely-sanctioned office below prophethood, receiving divine communication through a different mode.
